newsitem.title: GERMANY: German/S Africa air passengers seen up 8pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: German/S Africa air passengers seen up 8pct in '97.

text.p: German passenger demand for South Africa is set for eight percent growth this year, a South African Airways executive forecast.

Hans-Peter Fraembs, the airline's central Europe manager, said SAA expected the German passenger market for South Africa to grow about eight percent in 1997 after a 15 percent rise to 160,000 passengers in 1996.
Leisure travel was the fastest-growing segment and now accounted for 80 percent of seats while business travel was stagnating, he told Reuters in an interview.
Fraembs declined to disclose SAA passenger numbers from Germany but said Germany was the carrier's third largest market after Britain and the U.S..
Price-based competition in Germany from European airlines such as British Airways and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines which had virtually daily flights to South Africa was increasing, Fraembs said.
"The competition is killing prices. I would say there has been a 15 percent fall in European tariffs to South Africa over the last 18 months."
"This is a direct consequence of the total liberalisation of air travel to, from and within South Africa," he added.
The code-share alliance with Deutsche Lufthansa AG was clearly aimed at holding and extending the airlines' German market share, Fraembs said.
But he stressed the two carriers were not permitted to discuss tariff levels but only to coordinate flights, aircraft and joint marketing. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
